title: Writing seen in PHerc. 306B for the first time in 2000 years
summary: Vesuvius Challenge awarded a $50K First Letters Prize for scroll PHerc. 306B, where the winning submission reached the 10-character target and the papyrology team agreed on a reading, tentatively a Greek phrase with parallels in Aristotle and Philodemus. Ink was detected by multiplying two models (TRACE v3B and a fine-tuned A-hn). Letters remain faint, the readable area is small, and the work relied on hundreds of hours of manual labeling.
ai_technology: ML ink-detection models (TRACE v3B, A-hn) with VC3D GrowPatch

evidence.tested: The reading was checked by the papyrology team, which agreed on the letters with the winning submission, and was compared against 25 community submissions and a 10-character target; the page describes no independent replication.
evidence.unknown: The reading is partial and uncertain, letters remain faint, training on machine-generated labels could compound errors (not assessed), and the Grand Prize is not yet awarded.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning ink-detection models (TRACE v3B and a fine-tuned A-hn) produced the ink maps; the readings and prize review were done by humans.
